where it is stated as an adaptation of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>,
and we will actually need the immediate corollary that follows it.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 2.2</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>, <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>)<span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq{q}<p<\infty" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>q</mi><mo><</mo><mi>p</mi><mo><</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></math> and <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{0}>0" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>,
and let <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline"><mi>M</mi></math> be the Mazur map <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{p,q}" display="inline"><msub><mi>M</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub></math> scaled down by factor <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{p}{q}{C_{0}}^{p/q-1}" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mi>p</mi><mi>q</mi></mfrac><mo>⁢</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn><mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>.
Then for all <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in\ell_{p}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math> such that <math id="S2.Thmtheorem2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="||x||_{p},||y||_{p}\leq C_{0}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_left"><math id="S2.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tfrac{q}{p}(2C_{0})^{1-p/q}||x-y||_{p}^{p/q}\leq||M(x)-M(y)||_{q}\leq||x-y||_%
{p}." display="block"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mi>q</mi><mi>p</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>⁢</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 2.3</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2<p<\infty" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo><</mo><mi>p</mi><mo><</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></math>.
Every <math id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math>-point set <math id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\subset\ell_{p}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math> with diameter at most <math id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{0}>0" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>
admits an embedding <math id="S2.Thmtheorem3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f:X\to\ell_{2}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow></math> such that</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_left"><math id="S2.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\forall x,y\in X,\qquad\tfrac{2}{p}(2C_{0})^{1-p/2}\|x-y\|_{p}^{p/2}\leq\|f(x)%
-f(y)\|_{2}\leq\|x-y\|_{p}." display="block"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>⁢</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Proof of <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 1.3. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.3</span></a>.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta>0" display="inline"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, and let <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\subset\ell_{p}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math> be an <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math>-point metric space for <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(2,\infty)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
Construct a partition of <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline"><mi>X</mi></math> in the following steps:</p>
<ol id="S2.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Construct for <math id="S2.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline"><mi>X</mi></math> an <math id="S2.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(O(\log{n}),\log^{1/p}{n}\cdot\Delta/4)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-Lipschitz decomposition <math id="S2.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{init}}=\{K_{1},\ldots,K_{t}\}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
using <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 2.1 ([7]). ‣ 2.1 Lipschitz Decomposition in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟐,∞) ‣ 2 Decompositions and Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑>𝟐 ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Embed each cluster <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{i}\subset\ell_{p}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math> into <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>
using the embedding <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{K_{i}}" display="inline"><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup></math> provided by <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem3" title="Corollary 2.3. ‣ 2.1 Lipschitz Decomposition in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟐,∞) ‣ 2 Decompositions and Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑>𝟐 ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollary</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a> for <math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{0}:=\log^{1/p}{n}\cdot\Delta/4" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">For each embedded cluster <math id="S2.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{K_{i}}(K_{i})" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>,
construct an <math id="S2.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(O(\sqrt{\log{n}}),\frac{1}{2}\Delta/\log^{1/2-1/p}n)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⁢</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-Lipschitz decomposition <math id="S2.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}=\{K_{i}^{1},\ldots,K_{i}^{k_{i}}\}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
using <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite> and the JL Lemma <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S2.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">The final decomposition <math id="S2.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{out}}" display="inline"><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub></math> is obtained by taking the preimage of every cluster of every <math id="S2.I1.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}" display="inline"><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">It is easy to see that <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{out}}" display="inline"><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub></math> is indeed a partition of <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline"><mi>X</mi></math>,
consisting of <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{i=1}^{t}k_{i}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>t</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> clusters.
Next, consider <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in X" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> and let us bound <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr[P_{\text{out}}(x)\neq P_{\text{out}}(y)]" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
Observe that a pair of points can be separated only in steps 1 or 3.
Therefore,</p>
<table id="S5.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S2.Ex5"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\Pr" display="inline"><mi>Pr</mi></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\Big{[}P_{\text{out}}(x)\neq P_{\text{out}}(y)\Big{]}" display="inline"><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S2.Ex6"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\leq\Pr\Big{[}P_{\text{init}}(x)\neq P_{\text{init}}(y)\Big{]}+%
\Pr\Big{[}P_{i}(f^{K_{i}}(x))\neq P_{i}(f^{K_{i}}(y))\mid P_{\text{init}}(x)=P%
_{\text{init}}(y)=K_{i}\Big{]}" display="inline"><mrow><mi></mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S2.Ex7"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\leq O(\log{n})\frac{\|x-y\|_{p}}{\log^{1/p}{n}\cdot\Delta/4}+O(%
\sqrt{\log{n}})\frac{\|f^{K_{i}}(x)-f^{K_{i}}(y)\|_{2}}{\frac{1}{2}\Delta/\log%
^{1/2-1/p}n}" display="inline"><mrow><mi></mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⁢</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S2.Ex8"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\leq O(\log^{1-1/p}{n})\frac{\|x-y\|_{p}}{\Delta}," display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi></mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mfrac></mstyle></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
</table>
<p class="ltx_p">where the last inequality follows because each <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{K_{i}}" display="inline"><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup></math>
is non-expanding on its cluster <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{i}\subset\ell_{p}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">It remains to show that the final clusters all have diameter at most <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></math>.
Let <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in X" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> be in the same cluster, i.e., <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{out}}(x)=P_{\text{out}}(y)" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.
Then <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{init}}(x)=P_{\text{init}}(y)=K_{i}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}(f^{K_{i}}(x))=P_{i}(f^{K_{i}}(y))" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.
Combining the maximum possible diameter of <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{init}}(x)" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}(f^{K_{i}}(x))" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> with the contraction guarantees of <math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f=f^{K_{i}}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup></mrow></math>, we get</p>
<table id="S2.Ex9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_left"><math id="S2.Ex9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{2}{p}\Big{(}2(\log^{1/p}{n})\frac{\Delta}{4}\Big{)}^{1-p/2}\|x-y\|_{p}^{%
p/2}\leq\|f(x)-f(y)\|_{2}\leq\frac{\Delta}{2}\log^{1/p-1/2}{n}." display="block"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi></mfrac><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>⁢</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.167em">⁢</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
</table>
<p class="ltx_p">Rearranging this, we obtain
<math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|x-y\|_{p}\leq\frac{\sqrt[p/2]{p/2}}{2}\Delta\leq\Delta" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mfrac><mroot><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mroot><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⁢</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow></math>,
which completes the proof.
<math id="S2.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hfill\blacktriangleleft" display="inline"><mo>◀</mo></math></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Capped Decomposition in <math id="S2.SS2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ℓ</mi><mi>𝒑</mi></msub></math> for <math id="S2.SS2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(2,\infty)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>𝒑</mi><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">∈</mo><mrow><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟐</mn><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">,</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">∞</mi><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We now present our construction of capped decomposition,
which is a notion of decomposability
that was introduced in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite> without a concrete name.
We start with its definition, and then present our construction.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 2.4</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,\rho)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> be a metric space.
A distribution <math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></math> over partitions of <math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline"><mi>X</mi></math>
is called <em class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright"><math id="S2.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,\Delta,\eta)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped</em> if</span></p>
<ol id="S2.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S2.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S2.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">for every partition </span><math id="S2.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathcal{D})" display="inline"><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>supp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, all clusters </span><math id="S2.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C\in P" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> have </span><math id="S2.I2.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{diam}(C)\leq\Delta" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>diam</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">; and</span></p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S2.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S2.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">for every </span><math id="S2.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in X" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> such that </span><math id="S2.I2.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x,y)\leq\frac{\Delta}{t}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>t</mi></mfrac></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">,</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_left"><math id="S2.Ex10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr_{P\in\mathcal{D}}[P(x)=P(y)]\geq\eta." display="block"><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>Pr</mi><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></mrow></munder><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Observe that here, unlike in Lipschitz decomposition,
we have a guarantee on the probability that points <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in X" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> are clustered together
only if they are within distance <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\Delta}{t}" display="inline"><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>t</mi></mfrac></math> of each other,
hence the name “capped decomposition”.
Moreover, the probability bound does not depend on the exact value of <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x,y)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
We say that <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,\rho)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> admits a <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,\eta)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition, where <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=\eta(|X|,t)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>, if it admits a <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,\Delta,\eta)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition for every <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta>0" display="inline"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
A family of metrics admits a <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,\eta)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition
if every metric in the family admits a <math id="S2.SS2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,\eta)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 2.5</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(2,\infty)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
Then every <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math>-point metric in <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> admits
a <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,n^{-O(1/t^{q})})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition for all <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>,
where <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q\in(1,2)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is such that <math id="S2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>p</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>q</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Previously, such a decomposition was known only for the extreme case <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=2" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>
by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>, see <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem6" title="Proposition 2.6 ([22]). ‣ 2.2 Capped Decomposition in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟐,∞) ‣ 2 Decompositions and Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑>𝟐 ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Proposition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.6</span></a>,
and our bound above in fact converges to their bound when <math id="S2.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\to 2" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>.
Our proof of <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 2.5. ‣ 2.2 Capped Decomposition in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟐,∞) ‣ 2 Decompositions and Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑>𝟐 ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a>
is similar to <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 1.3. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.3</span></a>,
and relies on two known capped decompositions, that we introduce next,
together with the Mazur map <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem3" title="Corollary 2.3. ‣ 2.1 Lipschitz Decomposition in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟐,∞) ‣ 2 Decompositions and Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑>𝟐 ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollary</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 2.6</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>)<span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Every <math id="S2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math>-point subset of <math id="S2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> admits a <math id="S2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,n^{-O(1/t^{2})})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition for all <math id="S2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 2.7</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Implicit in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite>)<span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Every <math id="S2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math>-point metric space admits a <math id="S2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,n^{-O(1/t)})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition for all <math id="S2.Thmtheorem7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Proof of <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 2.5. ‣ 2.2 Capped Decomposition in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟐,∞) ‣ 2 Decompositions and Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑>𝟐 ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a>.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta>0" display="inline"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> and <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.
Let <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\subset\ell_{p}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math> be an <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math>-point subset of <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(2,\infty)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>,
where <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline"><mi>q</mi></math> is such that <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>p</mi></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>q</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.
Construct a partition of <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline"><mi>X</mi></math> in the following steps:</p>
<ol id="S2.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S2.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S2.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Construct for <math id="S2.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline"><mi>X</mi></math> a <math id="S2.I3.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t_{1}:=t^{q}/4,\Delta_{1}:=\Delta/4t^{1-q},n^{-O(1/t^{q})})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>q</mi></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition <math id="S2.I3.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{init}}=\{K_{1},\ldots,K_{t}\}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
using <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem7" title="Proposition 2.7 (Implicit in [39]). ‣ 2.2 Capped Decomposition in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟐,∞) ‣ 2 Decompositions and Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑>𝟐 ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Proposition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.7</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S2.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S2.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Embed each cluster <math id="S2.I3.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{i}\subset\ell_{p}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math> into <math id="S2.I3.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>
using the embedding <math id="S2.I3.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{K_{i}}" display="inline"><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup></math> provided by <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem3" title="Corollary 2.3. ‣ 2.1 Lipschitz Decomposition in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟐,∞) ‣ 2 Decompositions and Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑>𝟐 ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Corollary</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a> for <math id="S2.I3.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{0}:=\Delta_{1}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S2.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S2.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">For each embedded cluster <math id="S2.I3.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{K_{i}}(K_{i})" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
construct a <math id="S2.I3.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t_{2}:=t^{q/2}/2,\Delta_{2}:=\Delta/2t^{1-q/2},n^{-O(1/t^{q})})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition <math id="S2.I3.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}=\{K_{i}^{1},\ldots,K_{i}^{k_{i}}\}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
using <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem6" title="Proposition 2.6 ([22]). ‣ 2.2 Capped Decomposition in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟐,∞) ‣ 2 Decompositions and Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑>𝟐 ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Proposition</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.6</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S2.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S2.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">The final decomposition <math id="S2.I3.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{out}}" display="inline"><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub></math> is obtained by taking the preimage of every cluster of every <math id="S2.I3.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}" display="inline"><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">It is easy to see that that <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{out}}" display="inline"><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub></math> is indeed a partition of <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline"><mi>X</mi></math>,
consisting of <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{i=1}^{t}k_{i}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>t</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> clusters.
Next, consider <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in X" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> with <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|x-y\|_{p}\leq\Delta/t" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></math>
and let us bound <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr[P_{\text{out}}(x)=P_{\text{out}}(y)]" display="inline"><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
Observe that <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{1}/t_{1}=\Delta_{2}/t_{2}=\Delta/t" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></math>,
and therefore</p>
<table id="S5.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S2.Ex11"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\Pr" display="inline"><mi>Pr</mi></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\Big{[}P_{\text{out}}(x)=P_{\text{out}}(y)\Big{]}" display="inline"><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S2.Ex12"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\Pr\Big{[}P_{\text{init}}(x)=P_{\text{init}}(y)\Big{]}\cdot\Pr%
\Big{[}P_{i}(f^{K_{i}}(x))=P_{i}(f^{K_{i}}(y))\mid P_{\text{init}}(x)=P_{\text%
{init}}(y)=K_{i}\Big{]}" display="inline"><mrow><mi></mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em" rspace="0.055em">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S2.Ex13"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\geq n^{-O\left(1/t^{q}\right)}\cdot n^{-O\left(1/t^{q}\right)}=n%
^{-O\left(1/t^{q}\right)}," display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi></mi><mo>≥</mo><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>q</mi></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
</table>
<p class="ltx_p">where the inequality follows because each <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f^{K_{i}}" display="inline"><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup></math>
is non-expanding on its cluster <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{i}\subset\ell_{p}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">It remains to show that each cluster has diameter at most <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></math>.
Let <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in X" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> be in the same cluster, i.e., <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{out}}(x)=P_{\text{out}}(y)" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.
Then <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{init}}(x)=P_{\text{init}}(y)=K_{i}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> and <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}(f^{K_{i}}(x))=P_{i}(f^{K_{i}}(y))" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.
Combining the maximum possible diameter of <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\text{init}}(x)" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mtext>init</mtext></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{i}(f^{K_{i}}(x))" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> with the contraction guarantees of <math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f=f^{K_{i}}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>f</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msup></mrow></math>, we get</p>
<table id="S2.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_left"><math id="S2.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{2}{p}\Big{(}2\frac{\Delta}{4t^{1-q}}\Big{)}^{1-p/2}\|x-y\|_{p}^{p/2}\leq%
\|f(x)-f(y)\|_{2}\leq\frac{\Delta}{2t^{1-q/2}}." display="block"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mi>p</mi></mfrac><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></msup><mo>⁢</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
</table>
<p class="ltx_p">Rearranging this, we obtain
<math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|x-y\|_{p}\leq\frac{\sqrt[p/2]{p/2}}{2}\Delta\leq\Delta" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mfrac><mroot><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mroot><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⁢</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow></math>,
which completes the proof.
<math id="S2.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hfill\blacktriangleleft" display="inline"><mo>◀</mo></math></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.3 </span>Spanners in <math id="S2.SS3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ℓ</mi><mi>𝒑</mi></msub></math> for <math id="S2.SS3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(2,\infty)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>𝒑</mi><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">∈</mo><mrow><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟐</mn><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">,</mo><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">∞</mi><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
</h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We can now prove <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 1.4. ‣ Geometric Spanners for 𝒑≥𝟐. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.4</span></a>,
by applying the following spanner construction of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 2.8</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>)<span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S2.Thmtheorem8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,\rho)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> be an <math id="S2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math>-point metric space admitting a <math id="S2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,\eta)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>η</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition for some <math id="S2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.
Then, for every <math id="S2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\in(0,1/8)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>,
there exists a <math id="S2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(2+\epsilon)t" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>-spanner for <math id="S2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline"><mi>X</mi></math>
with <math id="S2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{\epsilon}(\frac{n}{\eta}\cdot\log n\cdot\log t)" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>n</mi><mi>η</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> edges
and lightness <math id="S2.Thmtheorem8.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O_{\epsilon}(\frac{t}{\eta}\cdot\log^{2}n)" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>O</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>t</mi><mi>η</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<section id="S2.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx1" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Proof of <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 1.4. ‣ Geometric Spanners for 𝒑≥𝟐. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.4</span></a>.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">The proof follows directly by combining <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 2.5. ‣ 2.2 Capped Decomposition in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟐,∞) ‣ 2 Decompositions and Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑>𝟐 ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a> and <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem8" title="Theorem 2.8 ([22]). ‣ 2.3 Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟐,∞) ‣ 2 Decompositions and Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑>𝟐 ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.8</span></a>,
as we can assume <math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=O(\log{n})" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> without loss of generality.
<math id="S2.SS3.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hfill\blacktriangleleft" display="inline"><mo>◀</mo></math></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Spanners in <math id="S3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">ℓ</mi><mi>𝒑</mi></msub></math> for <math id="S3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(1,2)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>𝒑</mi><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">∈</mo><mrow><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold" stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟏</mn><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">,</mo><mn>𝟐</mn><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">This section presents an improved construction of geometric spanners in <math id="S3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> for <math id="S3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(1,2)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
Previously, <math id="S3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(t)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>-spanners of size <math id="S3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(n^{1+\log^{2}{t}/t^{p}})" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> for all <math id="S3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>
were constructed in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>;
in particular, setting <math id="S3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=(\log{n}\log{\log{n}})^{1/p}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁢</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> yields
an <math id="S3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(t)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>-spanner of near-linear size <math id="S3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{O}(n)" display="inline"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>O</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
We first present in <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Spanners of Near-Linear Size ‣ 3 Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟏,𝟐) ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>
two different constructions of near-linear-size spanners with a slightly better stretch.
Then in <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Spanners with Stretch-Size Tradeoff ‣ 3 Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟏,𝟐) ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> we use yet another technique,
namely Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH),
to slightly improve the construction of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite> of spanners with general stretch <math id="S3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(t)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Spanners of Near-Linear Size</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We slightly improve the near-linear size spanner construction of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>
by shaving the <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\log\log{n})^{1/p}" display="inline"><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup></math> factor from the stretch, as follows.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 3.1</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For every fixed <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(1,2)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, every <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math>-point metric <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\subset\ell_{p}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math>
admits an <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log^{1/p}{n})" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>-spanner of size <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{O}(n)" display="inline"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>O</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We present two related but different proofs for this theorem.
Both are based on modifying the spanner algorithm for <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>,
and therefore we start with an overview of that algorithm.
Given an input set <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\subseteq\ell_{2}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>⊆</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math>,
the algorithm begins by constructing a hierarchical set of <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{i}" display="inline"><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>i</mi></msup></math>-nets
<math id="S3.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X=N_{0}\supseteq N_{1}\supseteq\cdots\supseteq N_{\log{\Delta_{X}}}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>⊇</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>⊇</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">⋯</mi><mo>⊇</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>X</mi></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></math>,
where we assume that the minimum and maximum distances in <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline"><mi>X</mi></math>
are <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline"><mn>1</mn></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{X}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>X</mi></msub></math>, respectively.
Then, for each level <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline"><mi>i</mi></math>, it constructs an <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(O(\sqrt{\log n}),O(\sqrt{\log n})\cdot 2^{i+1})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-Lipschitz decomposition of <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{i}" display="inline"><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>
by combining the JL Lemma <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite> with the Lipschitz decomposition of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>.
For each cluster in it, the algorithm add to the spanner edges in a star-like fashion,
meaning that all cluster points are connected to one arbitrary point within the cluster.
The last two steps are repeated <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log n)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> times
to ensure that with high probability, for each level <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline"><mi>i</mi></math>,
every <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in N_{i}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> with <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|x-y\|_{2}\leq 2^{i+1}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
are clustered together in at least one of the <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log n)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> repetitions.
It is shown in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite> that
this algorithm constructs an <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(O(\sqrt{\log{n}}))" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-spanner of size <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{O}(n)" display="inline"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>O</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1" class="ltx_subparagraph">
