<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Proof of <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3.1 Spanners of Near-Linear Size ‣ 3 Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟏,𝟐) ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> via Lipschitz Decomposition.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Observe that the above algorithm of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>
uses the fact that the points lie in <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>
only for the construction of Lipschitz Decompositions,
and relies on an optimal decomposition for finite <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> metrics
to conclude that the spanner’s stretch is <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\beta^{*}_{n}(\ell_{2}))" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>β</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
For finite <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> metrics, <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(1,2)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>,
we can use instead a Lipschitz decomposition from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>, <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>]</cite>,
which has <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=\frac{O(\log^{1/p}{n})}{p-1}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>,
to conclude the claimed stretch.
<math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hfill\blacktriangleleft" display="inline"><mo>◀</mo></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We next present a proof that modifies the algorithm of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite> differently,
and relies on a decomposition that is similar to a Lipschitz decomposition
but has slightly weaker guarantees.
Interestingly, this technique yields a slightly stronger result
than <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3.1 Spanners of Near-Linear Size ‣ 3 Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟏,𝟐) ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>,
where <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline"><mi>p</mi></math> need not to be fixed and can depend on <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math> (e.g., <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\to 1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>).
We proceed to introduce some technical results from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>
regarding a weak form of dimensionality reduction in <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math>,
for <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in[1,2]" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, which are needed for our proof.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 3.2</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite>)<span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,\rho)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(Y,\tau)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> be metric spaces
and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[a,b]" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math> be a real interval.
An embedding <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f:X\rightarrow Y" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></mrow></math>
is called <em class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright"><math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[a,b]" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>-range preserving with distortion <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\geq 1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> </em>
if there exists <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c>0" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> such that for all <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,x^{\prime}\in X" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></math>:</span></p>
<ol id="S3.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a\leq\rho(x,x^{\prime})\leq b" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, then </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x,x^{\prime})\leq c\cdot\tau(f(x),f(x^{\prime}))\leq D\cdot\rho(x,x^{%
\prime})" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If </span><math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x,x^{\prime})>b" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>></mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, then </span><math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\cdot\tau(f(x),f(x^{\prime}))\geq b" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S3.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If </span><math id="S3.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x,x^{\prime})<a" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo><</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, then </span><math id="S3.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c\cdot\tau(f(x),f(x^{\prime}))\leq D\cdot a" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We say that <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,\rho)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> admits <em class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">an <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline"><mi>R</mi></math>-range preserving embedding</em>
into <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(Y,\tau)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> with distortion <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline"><mi>D</mi></math>,
if for all <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u>0" display="inline"><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, there exists a <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[u,uR]" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>-range preserving embedding
into <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline"><mi>Y</mi></math> with distortion <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline"><mi>D</mi></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 3.3</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>)<span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq p\leq 2" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>. For every <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math>-point set <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\subset\ell_{p}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math>, and for every range parameter <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R>1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>, there exists an <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline"><mi>R</mi></math>-range preserving embedding <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f:S\rightarrow\ell_{p}^{k}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow></math> with distortion <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1+\epsilon" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></math>, such that <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=O\left(\frac{R^{O(1/\epsilon)}\cdot\log n}{\epsilon}\right)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mrow><mi>ϵ</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Proof of <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3.1 Spanners of Near-Linear Size ‣ 3 Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟏,𝟐) ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> via Weak Dimension Reduction.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Observe that the above algorithm of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>
only requires the decomposition of each net <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{i}" display="inline"><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>
to ensure that points <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in N_{i}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math> with <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|x-y\|_{2}\leq 2^{i+1}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>
are clustered together with constant probability,
and that the diameter of all clusters is at most <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\sqrt{\log{n}})\cdot 2^{i}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></math>;
of course, for <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\subset\ell_{p}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(1,2)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>,
we replace the <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\sqrt{\log{n}})" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></msqrt><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> factor with <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log^{1/p}{n})" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
A careful examination shows that these properties are preserved by first reducing the dimension using the range-preserving embedding provided by <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 3.3 ([9]). ‣ Proof of Theorem˜3.1 via Lipschitz Decomposition. ‣ 3.1 Spanners of Near-Linear Size ‣ 3 Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟏,𝟐) ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> with <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon=\frac{1}{2}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R=2" display="inline"><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>, and then constructing a Lipschitz decomposition for the image points in <math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}^{O(\log{n})}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup></math> using <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>.
<math id="S3.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hfill\blacktriangleleft" display="inline"><mo>◀</mo></math></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Spanners with Stretch-Size Tradeoff</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We now present, in <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 1.5. ‣ Geometric Spanners for 𝒑≤𝟐. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.5</span></a>,
a construction of <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(t)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>-spanners in <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math>, where <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(1,2)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>,
of size <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{O}(n^{1+1/t^{p}})" display="inline"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>O</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> for all <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>,
which slightly improves over the <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(t)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>-spanners of size <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{O}(n^{1+\log^{2}{t}/t^{p}})" display="inline"><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>O</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>.
It is worth noting that <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 1.5. ‣ Geometric Spanners for 𝒑≤𝟐. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.5</span></a>
generalizes the results of <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3.1 Spanners of Near-Linear Size ‣ 3 Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟏,𝟐) ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>,
and thus provides an alternative proof for it.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 3.4</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(LSH <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite>)<span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></math> be a family of hash functions mapping a metric <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,\rho)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> to some universe <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U" display="inline"><mi>U</mi></math>.
We say that <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></math> is <em class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright"><math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(r,tr,p_{1},p_{2})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-sensitive</em>
if for every <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in X" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></math>, the following is satisfied:</span></p>
<ol id="S3.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S3.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S3.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If </span><math id="S3.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x,y)\leq r" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, then </span><math id="S3.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr_{h\in\mathcal{H}}[h(x)=h(y)]\geq p_{1}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Pr</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S3.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S3.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If </span><math id="S3.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x,y)>tr" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>></mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, then </span><math id="S3.I2.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr_{h\in\mathcal{H}}[h(x)=h(y)]\leq p_{2}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Pr</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Such <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></math> is called an <em class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">LSH family</em>
with parameter <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma:=\frac{\log(1/p_{1})}{\log(1/p_{2})}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.5</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>)<span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,\rho)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> be a metric space such that for every <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r>0" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, there exists a <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(r,tr,p_{1},p_{2})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-sensitive LSH family with parameter <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline"><mi>γ</mi></math>. Then <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,\rho)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> admits a <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,n^{-\mathcal{O}(\gamma)})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">For <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=2" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>, the LSH family constructed in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>
can be used in <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma 3.5 ([22]). ‣ 3.2 Spanners with Stretch-Size Tradeoff ‣ 3 Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟏,𝟐) ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a>
to conclude that <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> admits
a <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,n^{-O(1/t^{2})})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition for every <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite>,
thereby proving <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 1.5. ‣ Geometric Spanners for 𝒑≤𝟐. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.5</span></a> for this case of <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=2" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>.
In a similar fashion,
an LSH family constructed in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite> for <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(1,2)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>
was used in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite> to show that these spaces admit a <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,n^{-O(\log^{2}{t}/t^{p})})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>log</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-capped decomposition.
We observe that this result can be improved by replacing the LSH family from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>,
with an alternative one that is briefly mentioned in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>,
and consequently prove <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 1.5. ‣ Geometric Spanners for 𝒑≤𝟐. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.5</span></a>.
For completeness, we reproduce this LSH family for <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math>, where <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(1,2)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.6</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>)<span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(1,2)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r>0" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, and large enough <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t>1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>. Then there exists a <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(r,tr,p_{1},p_{2})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-sensitive LSH family for <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> with parameter <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=\frac{1}{t^{p}}+o(1)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Proof.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in(1,2)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r>0" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>, and sufficiently large <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t>1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.
Let <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f:\ell_{p}\to\ell_{2}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow></math> be the isometric embedding of the <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(p/2)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-snowflake of <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> into <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>, Theorem 4.1]</cite>.
Take <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\prime}=r^{p/2}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{\prime}=t^{p/2}" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, and let <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></math> be the <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(r^{\prime},t^{\prime}r^{\prime},p_{1},p_{2})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-sensitive LSH family for <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> with parameter <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=\frac{1}{t^{\prime 2}}+o(1)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo mathsize="2.000em">′</mo><mo lspace="0em">⁣</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>. Observe that, for every <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in\ell_{p}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow></math>, if <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|x-y\|_{p}\leq r" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></math>, then <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|f(x)-f(y)\|_{2}=\|x-y\|_{p}^{p/2}\leq r^{p/2}=r^{\prime}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></math>, and thus</p>
<table id="S3.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_left"><math id="S3.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr_{h\in\mathcal{H}}[h(f(x))=h(f(y))]\geq p_{1}." display="block"><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>Pr</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow></munder><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
</table>
<p class="ltx_p">Similarly, if <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|x-y\|_{p}>tr" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>></mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></math>, then <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|f(x)-f(y)\|_{2}=\|x-y\|_{p}^{p/2}>(tr)^{p/2}=t^{\prime}r^{\prime}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>></mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></mrow></math>, and hence</p>
<table id="S3.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_left"><math id="S3.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr_{h\in\mathcal{H}}[h(f(x))=h(f(y))]\leq p_{2}." display="block"><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>Pr</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow></munder><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
</table>
<p class="ltx_p">We therefore conclude that <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}\circ f" display="inline"><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow></math> is an <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(r,tr,p_{1},p_{2})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-sensitive LSH family for <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> with parameter <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=\frac{1}{t^{p}}+o(1)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>p</mi></msup></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.
<math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hfill\blacktriangleleft" display="inline"><mo>◀</mo></math></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx2" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Proof of <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 1.5. ‣ Geometric Spanners for 𝒑≤𝟐. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.5</span></a>.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">The proof follows immediately by constructing a capped decomposition
based on <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma 3.5 ([22]). ‣ 3.2 Spanners with Stretch-Size Tradeoff ‣ 3 Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟏,𝟐) ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a> and <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem6" title="Lemma 3.6 ([4]). ‣ 3.2 Spanners with Stretch-Size Tradeoff ‣ 3 Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟏,𝟐) ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.6</span></a>,
and using it in the spanner construction from <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem8" title="Theorem 2.8 ([22]). ‣ 2.3 Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑∈(𝟐,∞) ‣ 2 Decompositions and Spanners in ℓ_𝒑 for 𝒑>𝟐 ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.8</span></a>.
<math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hfill\blacktriangleleft" display="inline"><mo>◀</mo></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacktriangleright" display="inline"><mo mathcolor="#4F4F54">▶</mo></math> <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">Remark 3.7</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">While <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>, Theorem 4.1]</cite> does not provide an efficiently computable embedding,
one can compute such an embedding for a finite set of points in polynomial time
by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Distance Labeling</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">In the distance labeling model,
a scheme is designed for an entire a family <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></math> of <math id="S4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math>-point metrics
(and in some scenarios, all these metrics have the same point set <math id="S4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline"><mi>X</mi></math>,
e.g., different graphs on the same vertex set).
A <em class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">scheme</em> is an algorithm that preprocesses each metric <math id="S4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline"><mi>X</mi></math> in <math id="S4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></math>
and assigns to each point <math id="S4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in X" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> a label <math id="S4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l(x)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 4.1</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">A scheme is <em class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">a distance labeling</em>
with approximation <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\geq 1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> and label size of <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline"><mi>k</mi></math> if</span></p>
<ol id="S4.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">every label (for every point in every metric in </span><math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">)
consists of at most </span><math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline"><mi>k</mi></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> bits; and</span></p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">there is an algorithm </span><math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> that, given the labels </span><math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l(x),l(y)" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">
of two points </span><math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> in a metric </span><math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,\rho)\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">
(but not given </span><math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,\rho)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> or the points </span><math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">),
outputs an estimate </span><math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}(l(x),l(y))" display="inline"><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> that satisfies</span></p>
<table id="S4.Ex17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_left"><math id="S4.Ex17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x,y)\leq\mathcal{A}(l(x),l(y))\leq D\cdot\rho(x,y)." display="block"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_left_padright"></td>
</tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">The following theorem was presented in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite> with limited details,
and we include a proof of it below for completeness.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 4.2</span></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>)<span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span>
</h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></math> be a family of <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math>-point metrics,
and assume that all the pairwise distances in all metrics <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,\rho)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> in <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></math>
are in the range <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[1,\Delta_{\text{max}}]" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">max</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></math>.
Then <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></math> admits a distance-labeling scheme
with approximation <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\beta^{*}(\mathcal{X}))" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>β</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and label size <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\log n\log\Delta_{\max})" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁢</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> bits.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">It is straightforward to see that <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem6" title="Theorem 1.6. ‣ Distance Labeling Schemes. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.6</span></a>
follows by combining <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 4.2 ([24]). ‣ 4 Distance Labeling ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>
and <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 1.3. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Proof of <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 4.2 ([24]). ‣ 4 Distance Labeling ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We first describe the preprocessing algorithm,
denoting <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta:=\beta^{*}(\mathcal{X})" display="inline"><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>β</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.
Perform the following steps for all levels <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=0,\ldots,\log{\Delta_{\text{max}}}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mtext>max</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.
Begin by constructing a <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\beta,\Delta_{i}:=4\beta 2^{i})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:=</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-Lipschitz decomposition,
and observe that every two points <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y\in X" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow></math> with <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x,y)\leq 2^{i}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>i</mi></msup></mrow></math> are separated with probability at most <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{4}" display="inline"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>.
Then, assign a random bit to each cluster,
and observe that if two points are at distance greater than <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{i}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math>,
they always fall in different clusters,
hence, the probability that they are assigned the same bit is exactly <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{2}" display="inline"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>, and if they are at distance at most <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{i}=\Delta_{i}/(4\beta)" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>i</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>
they are assigned the same bit with probability at least <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{3}{4}" display="inline"><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math>.
Repeat the last two steps <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=O(\log{n})" display="inline"><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math> times,
and then with high probability, every two points <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x,y" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></math> are assigned
the same bit at least <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{5}{8}k" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>⁢</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> times if <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x,y)\leq\Delta_{i}/(4\beta)" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>
and fewer than <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{5}{8}k" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>⁢</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> times if <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x,y)>\Delta_{i}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>></mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math>.
Finally, label each point by concatenating the bit assigned to its cluster
in all the repetitions at all levels.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">The label-size analysis is straightforward.
It remains to show that, given two labels <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l(x),l(y)" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>,
it is possible to approximate the distance <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho(x,y)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> within factor <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O(\beta)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
This can be achieved by identifying the smallest level <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline"><mi>i</mi></math>
such that <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline"><mi>y</mi></math> are assigned the same bit at least <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{5}{8}k" display="inline"><mrow><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>⁢</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> times,
and then the above analysis (used in contrapositive form) implies that
<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{i-1}/(4\beta)<\rho(x,y)\leq\Delta_{i}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo><</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></math>,
where by convention <math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{-1}:=1" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.
<math id="S4.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hfill\blacktriangleleft" display="inline"><mo>◀</mo></math></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Future Directions</h2>

<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Lipschitz Decompositions.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We stress that our decomposition in <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 1.3. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.3</span></a>
employs a data-dependent approach, and is not oblivious to the input set <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline"><mi>X</mi></math>
(as, say, the decomposition for <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>,
even when applied together with the JL Lemma).
In retrospect, this feature is perhaps not very surprising,
because data-dependent approaches have been already shown to be effective
for central problems, such as nearest neighbor search <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite>.
We thus mention that a major open problem in the field
is whether dimension reduction is possible in <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> for <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\neq 1,2,\infty" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></mrow></math>;
we know that for <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p>2" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>></mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> this is not possible via an oblivious mapping <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>,
raising the question whether data-dependent mappings can overcome this limitation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Geometric Spanners.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">The geometric spanners in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>, <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite> for <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math>, <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1<p\leq 2" display="inline"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo><</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math>,
are not known to be optimal, i.e., we do not know of matching lower bounds,
except for the more restricted case of <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline"><mn>2</mn></math>-hop spanners <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>.
We conjecture that tight instances exist in these spaces,
i.e., the spanner bounds obtained in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>, <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite> are optimal for every stretch <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline"><mi>t</mi></math>.
We similarly do not know of matching lower bounds
for the geometric spanners in <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math>, for fixed <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\leq p<\infty" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>p</mi><mo><</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></math>,
that we obtain in <a href="#S1.Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 1.4. ‣ Geometric Spanners for 𝒑≥𝟐. ‣ 1.1 Our Results ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Lipschitz Decompositions of Finite ℓ_𝑝 Metrics" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.4</span></a>,
and it is quite plausible that our upper bounds are not tight.
We do know however, based on known results, that for every <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math>,
there exist tight instances in <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{p}" display="inline"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></math> for <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=\Omega(\log{n})" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
